title: World Calendar
intro: The World Calendar is a proposed reform of Gregorian civil dating with four identical quarterly structures.
structure: Each quarter contains three months of 31, 30 and 30 days, making 91 ordinary days or thirteen complete weeks. Four quarters provide 364 ordinary days. World Day follows the final quarter; a leap day follows June in Gregorian leap years. The proposal excludes these intercalary days from the ordinary weekly cycle.
model: The provider represents the reform proposal with explicit intercalary days and Gregorian year alignment. Ordinary month dates and special days must be distinguished in conversion and navigation.
example: January, April, July and October each begin a 31-day month; the following two months in each quarter have 30 days. The quarterly pattern repeats four times before World Day.
history: Reformers proposed the equal-quarter calendar to simplify annual scheduling and accounting. Its interruption of the continuous seven-day week was controversial, and it was not adopted as a universal civil chronology.
limits: This resource models a proposed calendar, not a record of widespread historical adoption. Special day conventions differ from Gregorian date and weekday rules.
